notes: Full description: pkix-revocation/src/ocsp.rs check_revocation() lines 182-190. When now_unix < produced_at (the OCSP response claims to have been produced in the future), the code returns Err(Error::OcspStatusUnknown). OcspStatusUnknown per the doc comment means 'The OCSP responder returned an unknown status (hard-fail mode)'. But the actual condition here is a validity window failure, not an unknown status. The same validity-window logic in check_revocation returns OcspStatusUnknown for thisUpdate > now (line 192-195) and nextUpdate < now (line 198-205), so the pattern is consistent within ocsp.rs. However, CrlChecker returns Error::CrlExpired for its time-window failures, while OcspChecker returns OcspStatusUnknown. This creates an asymmetry: callers who want to distinguish 'cert status unknown' from 'OCSP response is stale/future-dated' cannot do so from OcspChecker. Fix: Add a new Error variant (e.g., OcspExpired or OcspNotYetValid) for validity window failures, or return the existing OcspMalformed variant (since a response from the future is structurally suspicious). The security is not affected (fail-closed), but diagnostic quality suffers. Priority: P3 (diagnostic/error quality).
title: FINDING: OcspChecker returns OcspStatusUnknown for future producedAt (wrong error)
